newsitem.title: CANADA: Pacific Forest, Avenor up on sale plans.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Forest, Avenor up on sale plans.

text.p: Pacific Forest Products Ltd shares rose on Friday after the lumber company said that it was up for sale.

Shares in Montreal-based Avenor Inc, which owns 53 percent of the company, also gained. Avenor and Pacific Forest said late on Thursday that they would look for buyers for the whole company and also explore the idea of turning Pacific Forest into a timberland income fund.
Pacific Forest shares were up 0.95 to 24.25 in Toronto, while Avenor stock advanced 0.50 to 22.20.
With about 19.7 million shares outstanding, Pacific Forest's market capitalization was around C$478 million.
The move had been expected after Avenor said earlier this year it would divest its British Columbia assets as part of its C$2.75 billion merger with Repap Enterprises Inc.

Analysts said it appeared likely that transforming Pacific Forest into a royalty trust would generate the highest return to shareholders. TimberWest Forest Ltd was the first British Columbia company to try the technique when it recently announced such a deal, saying it would yield a higher price than the outright sale of the company.

"I think they will probably go the income-trust route...because by selling these facilities (outright) they don't seem to be able to get the value they want," said Loewen Ondaatje analyst John Carroll.

Analysts said they expected the company to fetch a higher value than its current market price, but they doubted the premium would be as much as the 40 percent difference between TimberWest's share price before its sale process was announced and the value of its ultimate royalty-trust deal.
They noted that Pacific Forest stock had already climbed close to 40 percent from around 18 in December when the Avenor/Repap merger was announced.
News that Avenor would divest its B.C. operations was part of that announcement.
Pacific Forest operates three sawmills and has privately owned timberlands. In 1996 it earned C$21.5 million on sales of C$383.6 million.

Salman Partners analyst Sam Magid said he was recommending clients take profits on the rise in Pacific Forest stock even though some industry observers speculate that the shares could fetch C$30 in an income-trust spinoff.

Fundamentals for the company do not justify a higher price and part of the trading on Friday was a kneejerk reaction to news of the proposed sale. Moreover, jittery debt markets may make an income trust deal harder to orchestrate, he said.
"At C$24.50 it is fully valued...There is no corporate buyer who will pay these kind of prices," he said.
